questions.knowledge_point: Calculating dy/dx at a Point Using dx/dy
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{5}+3y-5) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{5})+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)-5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(1) \\  & =5{y}^{4}+3(1)+0 \\  & =5{y}^{4}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{5{y}^{4}+3}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(33,2),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(33,2)} & =\frac{1}{5\cdot {2}^{4}+3}=\frac{1}{83}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Tangent Line Using dx/dy
questions.problem: Given a curve $x=5{y}^{5}-3{y}^{3},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-2,-1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(5{y}^{5}-3{y}^{3}) \\  & =5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{5})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3}) \\  & =5\cdot (5{y}^{4})-3\cdot (3{y}^{2}) \\  & =25{y}^{4}-9{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{25{y}^{4}-9{y}^{2}}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-2,-1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(-2,-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{25(-1)^{4}-9(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-1) & =\frac{1}{16}(x-(-2)) \\ y+1 & =\frac{1}{16}(x+2) \\ y & =\frac{x}{16}+\frac{2}{16}-1 \\ y & =\frac{x}{16}+\frac{1}{8}-1 \\ y & =\frac{x}{16}-\frac{7}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Tangent Line Using dx/dy
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(3y-{y}^{2}) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =3(1)-2y \\  & =3-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{3-2y}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(0,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(0,3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{3-2(3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-3)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =-\frac{1}{3}\cdot (x-0) \\ y & =-\frac{1}{3}x+3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating dy/dx at a Point Using dx/dy
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(4{y}^{4}-3y) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{4})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y) \\  & =4(4{y}^{3})-3 \\  & =16{y}^{3}-3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{16{y}^{3}-3}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(1,1),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(1,1)} & =\frac{1}{16({1}^{3})-3}=\frac{1}{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating dy/dx at a Point Using dx/dy
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-\frac{16}{\sqrt[3]{y}}+13) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-16{y}^{-1/3}+13) \\  & =-16\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1/3})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(13) \\  & =-16(-\frac{1}{3}{y}^{-4/3})+0 \\  & =\frac{16}{3}{y}^{-4/3} \\  & =\frac{16}{3{(\sqrt[3]{y})}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{3{(\sqrt[3]{y})}^{4}}{16}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(5,8),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(5,8)} & =\frac{3{(\sqrt[3]{8})}^{4}}{16} \\  & =\frac{3(16)}{16} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
